title: Cavalaire, Pardigon bay and the memory of the landing
author: Caramagnols
excerpt: Cavalaire-sur-Mer is not read only as an open bay. Pardigon, archaeology and the memory of the landing give the walk a depth that is not always seen at first glance.
content:
Cavalaire-sur-Mer first appears very simple: a broad bay, a shoreline and a town turned towards the sea. Yet as soon as one considers Pardigon and the memory of the landing, the walk gains another layer.

The bay as the first obvious feature

The bay immediately gives the landscape its breadth. It opens space, loosens the reading of the coastline and places Cavalaire in a broader relation to the gulf than many tighter communes.

Pardigon and older traces

The Pardigon sector reminds you that the shoreline is older than recent resort life. Archaeology reveals a deeper history of occupation and use that goes far beyond the contemporary seaside town alone.

The landing as part of coastal memory

The memory of the landing gives the landscape a particular gravity. It does not erase the bay or the present walk, but it obliges one to read the shore as a place of history as much as a summer space.

This note extends the page Walking Through Cavalaire-sur-Mer. To continue within the same cluster, it also helps to open Gigaro, Cap Lardier and Cap Taillat from La Croix-Valmer.
